page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-8GB is a compute-focused instance within UpCloud's Cloud Native series, provisioned via the KVM hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, configured with 1 thread per core across 4 physical cores. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware cache configuration consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. Standard instruction set flags include AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, whereas AVX-512 extensions and AMX matrix instructions are absent. No dedicated GPU hardware or local disk storage is bundled with this instance type, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark results demonstrate intermediate processing capability with notable constraints under sustained load. In Geekbench testing, the server achieved a single-core score of 1484.0 and a multi-core score of 5232.0, aligning with median results for its core count. PassMark CPU testing logged an overall score of 8006.57, including 6837.42 in extended instructions and 4589.96 in cryptographic tasks. Synthetic stress testing reveals hardware limits under saturation: stress-ng single-core performance recorded 782.69 points (bottom 10 percentile), while multi-core yielded 3106.23 points (bottom 25 percentile). Memory throughput shows 398.82 GB/sec for small cached blocks, declining to 40.7 GB/sec read and 23.27 GB/sec write for uncached 256 MB buffers, resulting in a PassMark memory score of 1606.27.

Due to its shared CPU allocation model and absence of bundled local NVMe storage, the CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-8GB represents an entry-level, budget-conscious configuration. It exhibits weak throughput in high-concurrency tasks such as Redis SET commands (5.58 million operations per second) and static web serving (4.22 GB/sec). Consequently, this instance type is best matched with low-to-moderate utility workloads, light CI/CD workers, development and testing environments, and non-critical distributed web services that do not require dedicated core access or sustained vector computation.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-8GB is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 8.0 GB of system memory. Hypervised through KVM, the configuration delivers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio alongside a 16 MB L3 cache, basic AVX, and hardware AES acceleration. There is no bundled GPU accelerator, local disk storage, or default public IPv4 allocation. Performance benchmarks place general processing in the median category, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5232.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8006.57. However, shared-core provisioning limits sustained execution, showing bottom-quartile results in stress-ng stress runs, uncached memory writes, and Redis throughput. This server is best suited for entry-level container workloads, lightweight CI/CD builds, and non-critical development environments.
